title: Strings
body:
A finite sequence of symbols drawn from an [[Alphabet]] $\Sigma$. Length is written $|w|$.

- $\varepsilon$ is the **empty string**, length 0. It is a string, not nothing, and forgetting
  that is where half the [[DFA]] mistakes come from.
- $\Sigma^*$ is the set of *all* strings over $\Sigma$, including $\varepsilon$. It is
  infinite even when $\Sigma$ has one symbol.
- $\Sigma^+ = \Sigma^* \setminus \{\varepsilon\}$.
- Concatenation $xy$ just glues them: $|xy| = |x| + |y|$, and $w\varepsilon = \varepsilon w = w$.
- $w^n$ is $w$ repeated $n$ times, with $w^0 = \varepsilon$. This is the notation the
  [[Pumping Lemma]] runs on.

Nothing to do with the C [[String]] type: no null terminator, no memory, just a mathematical
sequence.

[[Languages]] · [[INTRODUCTION TO COMPUTABILITY]]
